svg.desc: Banner for a paper on renewal resetting of quantum dynamics. A qubit evolves under a gate and is reset at random renewal times. Left: the exponent alpha in the reset hazard r_n = gamma/(n+1)^alpha decides the long-time state. Three traces show the coherence 2 Re rho_01 for the gate U = diag(1, −1), reset state |+⟩ and gamma = 1/4, for steps t = 1 to 500 on a logarithmic time axis, computed exactly from the model. For alpha below 1 (here alpha = 0, a constant hazard; finite mean waiting time) the coherence converges to a survival-weighted mixture, here the value 1/7. For alpha = 1 (proper clock with infinite mean waiting time) the oscillation shrinks slowly towards zero: the state dephases to D_U(rho). For alpha above 1 (here alpha = 2; a defective clock, with probability q = 2/pi of never resetting) the oscillation persists: the state approaches a rotating orbit and converges only if the reset state commutes with the gate. A footnote states that in finite dimension every gate and reset state converge exactly when the clock is proper and aperiodic. Right: at alpha = 1, the coherence decays as t to the power −min{gamma, 1 − gamma}, drawn as a tent over gamma from 0 to 1 with peak exponent 1/2 at gamma = 1/2. Dots mark the paper’s estimates of the number of steps until a pi-phase qubit coherence stays below 1%: 6.4 thousand at gamma = 1/2 and 2.3 × 10^9 at gamma = 0.2 or 0.8. These are two-term asymptotic estimates from the paper’s time-scale table; the value at 1/2 was also checked by the exact recurrence.
